contents.name: §3.4.1 Motivation for the surgery step: attaching a single cell, π_l(f')=π_l(f) for l≤k, and the epimorphism π_{k+1}(f)→π_{k+1}(f') whose kernel contains ω (Zπ_1(Y)-submodule generated by ω for k≥3)
§3.4.1 manifold modification: M' = (M − int(im(q))) ∪ D^{k+1}×S^{n-k-1}, straightening the angle, and the bordism W = D^{k+1}×D^{n-k} ∪_q M×[0,1]
§3.4.1 the modification does not affect π_l(f) for l≤k and gives an epimorphism on π_{k+1} with kernel containing ω, provided 2(k+1) ≤ n
§3.4.1 existence of the extension of the embedding q: S^k×D^{n-k}→M is equivalent to triviality of the normal bundle of the embedded sphere; if 2k ≤ n−1 then ν(S^k,M) is trivial
§3.4.1 the smooth structure on the glued manifold requires straightening the angle; the boundary M−int(im(q)) is glued to D^{k+1}×S^{n-k-1} along S^k×S^{n-k-1}

§3.4.2 Immersions and embeddings: Theorem 3.56 (Whitney approximation by immersions/embeddings), Theorem 3.57 (immersion classification by bundle monomorphisms), Example 3.58 (π_0 Imm(S²,R³) is a point)
contents.reason: Owned by the DG Whitney embedding/tubular page and by the immersion, regular-homotopy and sphere-eversion pages of this run; this page builds surgery only from a supplied framed embedding and needs no immersion classification.

contents.name: Lemma 3.55 (finite generation of the kernel module of a map of finite CW complexes, and killing by finitely many cells)
contents.reason: Finiteness and finite generation belong with the inductive below-middle surgery engine; this page analyses a single surgery step and makes no finiteness claim.

contents.name: Theorem 3.59 (The Surgery Step), parts (1)–(4): the commutative bundle diagram, uniqueness of the regular homotopy class, embeddings in the class, and the normal map on the trace W extending (f, f), with the effect M' normally bordant to M
Definition 3.60 (the result of surgery on a normal map; the surgery step) and Example 3.58-style discussion of the surgery step's effect
Theorem 3.61 (a finite sequence of surgery steps makes a degree-one normal map k-connected for n=2k or 2k+1, normally bordant to the original)
contents.reason: The inductive engine producing high connectivity by finitely many surgeries is the content of the following Whitney-trick/surgery page; this page does not use finiteness.

contents.name: Problem 3.62 (the surgery problem: can a normal map be changed to a homotopy equivalence by finitely many surgery steps?)
Remark 3.63, first sentence: the surgery step does not change the normal bordism class
Remark 3.63, signature consequence: in dimension 4k the difference sign(M) − sign(X) is a normal-bordism invariant and an obstruction
contents.reason: Signature and its oriented-homotopy invariance are owned by the in-run Hirzebruch-signature pair (order 555); this page does not define signature or its L-polynomial.

contents.name: Definition 3.50 and Lemma 3.51 (normal maps with respect to the tangent bundle and to the normal bundle, and the natural bijection between the two bordism sets)
Theorem 3.52 (Normal maps and G/O: canonical bijections [M,G/O] ≅ T_n(M) ≅ N_n(M) ≅ N^T_n(M))
contents.reason: The G/O classification of normal maps is not part of the commissioned level of this page, which records the normal-map input and its bordism relation only; no item consumes the classifying space.

contents.name: Problem 3.54 (change a given normal map into a normal map which is a homotopy equivalence)
§4.1 the intersection pairing λ: I_k(M)×I_k(M)→Zπ (4.1) and Lemma 4.3 (symmetry and linearity)
contents.reason: Geometric intersection pairings of immersed spheres are owned by the in-run DT-12 pair, which proves the pairing, its algebraic model and its Euler-class identification; this page only cites the form's existence and the middle-dimensional obstruction.

contents.name: §4.1 Remark 4.4 (λ(f,f)=0 is necessary for an embedding in the regular homotopy class of an immersion with a nowhere vanishing normal section)
§4.1.2 the self-intersection element μ (4.6) and Lemma 4.7 (the relation between λ, μ and the Euler number of the normal bundle)
contents.reason: The self-intersection form μ is the core of the Whitney-trick machinery assigned to the following page of this run; this page records only that the obstruction exists and is not developed here.

contents.name: §4.1 Theorem 4.8 (for k≥3 a pointed immersion S^k↬M^{2k} is pointed regularly homotopic to an embedding if and only if μ(f,w)=0)
contents.reason: This is the representability theorem proved by the Whitney trick on the following page; this page cites only the qualitative obstruction and the dimension condition.

contents.name: §4.1 Remark 4.9 (dim M ≥ 5 gives k ≥ 3 and permits an embedded Whitney disk; for k=2 only an immersion is available, which is the technical reason why surgery in dimension 4 is much more complicated)
Chapter 4 introduction (the surgery obstruction takes values in L-groups defined by forms and formations; the completion problem)

Proposition 10.2, dual reading: the same trace supports the surgery and its dual, so the two operations are mutually inverse along the trace
Corollary 10.3 (for 2n+2 ≤ m an n-connected map can be made (n+1)-connected by n-surgeries iff finitely many module generators can be killed)
Definition 10.4 (framing obstruction ν(φ)=ν_g∈π_n(BO(m−n))) and Proposition 10.5 (killability iff representable by a framed n-embedding iff the framing obstruction vanishes)

contents.reason: The regular-homotopy groups of immersions are the immersion-theoretic approach to surgery used by the following page; this page needs only the elementary map and bundle extension of a single surgery step.

contents.reason: Kernel modules over the group ring are the language of the target-map surgery engine and of the h-cobordism handle algebra; this page computes ordinary homology and homotopy groups of the trace instead.

contents.reason: These are the structural results of the kernel-module approach, consumed by the below-middle surgery and h-cobordism pages; no item of this page uses the kernel modules.

§10.4 Proposition 10.24 (for 2n+1 ≤ m an element x∈π_n(M) can be killed by n-surgery iff it is representable by an embedding with trivial normal bundle)
§10.4 Proposition 10.25 (i)-(iv) (killing elements below the middle; the exact sequences of kernel modules for 2n+2<m, m=2n+2 and m=2n+1)

contents.name: §7.1 definition of a simple surgery, or spherical modification, of type (r,m−r+1); M' has the same boundary as M; if M' is obtained from M by type (r,m−r+1) then M is obtained from M' by type (m−r+1,r), with the same supporting manifold
§7.1 the supporting manifold W = (M×I) ∪_f h^r with ∂_−W=M, ∂_+W=M' and ∂_cW = ∂M×I
§7.1 up to homotopy W is obtained from M by attaching an r-cell and from M' by attaching an (m−r+1)-cell; the intersection X = M∩M' and the four pairs (M,X), (M',X), (W,M), (W,M')
§7.1 the modification gives a manifold M' with the same boundary as M, and the boundary of the complement of the attaching region is glued to the outgoing region D^r×S^{m−r}

§7.1 extension of f over the handle is equivalent to a map g:D^r→X restricting to f∘φ_0 on the boundary; the pair (φ,f) defines an element of π_r(f); normal map definition (f:M→X, ν over X, trivialisation of TM⊕f^*ν); Theorem 7.1.1 (a regular homotopy class of immersions, and surgery on an embedding gives another normal map)

§7.1 conditions on ξ∈π_r(f): ∂ξ must be represented by an embedding, the normal bundle must be trivial, and for m≥2r−1 stable triviality of the normal bundle (equivalently triviality of TM restricted to the sphere) suffices
§7.1 Lemma 7.1.2 (M and M' have the same (r−2)-type; if r<m−r and x is the homology class of the a-sphere then H_{r−1}(M') is the quotient of H_{r−1}(M) by the subgroup generated by x)
§7.1 Proposition 7.1.3 (the exact sequences obtained from the four pairs (M,X), (M',X), (W,M), (W,M') for i<m−1)
§7.1 the modification is determined by φ and only by its diffeotopy class (Theorem 2.4.2); the two disk-factor decompositions of ∂(D^r×D^{m-r})
§7.2 Theorem 7.2.1 (X a finite CW complex, m≥2k: any normal map is normally cobordant to a k-connected normal map) and Corollary 7.2.2 (stably trivial tangent bundle: surgery makes M (k−1)-connected)
contents.reason: The inductive construction making maps highly connected by finitely many surgeries is the content of the following page of this run; this page analyses a single surgery step and its effect.

contents.name: §7.2 Theorem 7.2.3 and Corollary 7.2.4 (embeddings S^{m−2}⊂S^m with prescribed complement and the characterisation of their fundamental groups for m≥5)
